title: The Crimson Court - Gothic Vampire Castle Waltz and Harpsichord Game Music Pack - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track gothic vampire castle score: 16 real waltzes, a harpsichord in every track. MIDI + OGG, loop tagged.
description:
The Crimson Court is a 44 track gothic vampire castle music pack for games: 38 full looping pieces and 6 short cues, 45:24 of music, as OGG files with sample accurate loop tags plus all 44 editable MIDI sources. RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop points with no plugin, and the Readme gives the import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Royalty free for commercial games. Three full tracks are free to download on this page, with their MIDI.

One night at a vampire's court, from the carriage through the pass to dawn over the castle. The arrival: The Crimson Court, Carriage Through the Pass, The Village Below the Castle, The Castle Gates and The Grand Staircase. The ball: The Ballroom, The Countess Waltz, The Masquerade, A Dance with a Stranger, The Chandelier, The Midnight Banquet and The Music Room. The castle by night: The Portrait Gallery, The Library of Ash, The Clock Tower, The Chapel Profaned, The Alchemist's Tower, The Armoury, The Courtyard by Moonlight and The Rose Garden. Below the castle: The Crypt, The Catacombs, The Dungeon of Chains, The Flooded Cistern and The Blood Fountain. The hunt: The Hunt Begins, Wolves in the Black Forest, The Ramparts, The Bell Tower Stairs, The Night Watch and The Hunter Hunted. The masters of the court: The Countess Awakens and Dance of the Crimson Countess. Rest and dawn: The Last Dance, Dawn over the Castle, Candlelight, The Empty Ballroom and The Court Adjourns. Cues: The Stake Strikes, Drained, A Coffin's Rest, A Hidden Passage, They Know You Are Here and A Relic of the Old Blood.

Real waltzes. 16 of the tracks are waltzes in 3/4, the ballroom set and its echoes around the castle: The Village Below the Castle, The Grand Staircase, The Ballroom, The Countess Waltz, The Masquerade, A Dance with a Stranger, The Chandelier, The Midnight Banquet, The Music Room, The Courtyard by Moonlight, The Rose Garden, The Blood Fountain, Dance of the Crimson Countess, The Last Dance, The Empty Ballroom and The Court Adjourns. On every one the accompaniment is written the way a waltz is: across the 557 bars of their loops the bass plays exactly one note per bar, on the downbeat (the chord root 317 times and its fifth 240 times), and the pad plays the chord on beats two and three, 2,228 notes, every one a tone of the chord sounding then. Checked bar by bar in the shipped MIDI: 557 of 557.

One castle's sound. The harpsichord plays in all 44 tracks, 1,670 notes: it leads 5 of them and carries the counter line or the colour in the rest, so every room shares one instrument as well as one theme.

The Neapolitan chord. Every one of the 17 full pieces in harmonic minor uses the Neapolitan chord in its second half, the major chord on the lowered second degree (in D minor, E flat major), which moves to the dominant and then home to the tonic. 17 of them on the record, and all three tones of each one sound in the accompaniment, 17 of 17, measured.

One theme, every track. The seed theme, Crimson, reaches up a fifth on a long note and sighs back down by step, and all 44 tracks state it in its own shape, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI. Four more themes come from it: Sanguine is the seed turned over, for the crypt and the catacombs; Nocturne is the lament, for the music room and the last dance; Masque is the dance itself; Hunt runs in eighths for the chase. 1,118 statements and fragments of the 5 themes across the album.

What is in it. 38 full pieces and 6 short cues, 45:24 of music, 20 in harmonic minor, 12 in aeolian, 7 in dorian and 5 in ionian, 29 keys, 56 to 176 BPM, 16 in 3/4 and 28 in 4/4. 30 General MIDI instruments, among them harpsichord, organ, harp, timpani, choir, music box and tubular bells. Every pitched note is in its track's mode or a tone of a chord the track declares: 17,378 notes read, none outside those two.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 38 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read; each looping file ends exactly at its loop end. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

Gate results. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: The Ballroom, a waltz, The Hunt Begins, the chase, and Dance of the Crimson Countess, the final boss, which is a waltz too.

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, so the harpsichord, organ and strings are the General MIDI sounds of those names; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace them. No game cue, waltz or song is quoted; every tune was composed for this record. The castle and its court are invented. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: The Crimson Court is out: a 44 track vampire castle score with 16 real waltzes
devlog.body:
The Crimson Court is a 44 track gothic vampire castle score for games: one night at the court, from the carriage through the pass to dawn over the castle, with the ballroom, the countess, the portrait gallery, the crypt, the hunt, two bosses and the cues a game fires all day. It is live now, with three full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. 16 of the tracks are real waltzes (one bass note on every downbeat, the chord on beats two and three, 557 of 557 bars checked), the harpsichord plays in all 44, and every harmonic minor piece uses the Neapolitan chord on its way home. Each of those is counted in the shipped MIDI, and the seed theme is stated in its own shape in all 44 tracks.

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. The loop tags were followed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks (The Ballroom, The Hunt Begins and Dance of the Crimson Countess) are for.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace the sounds. No game cue or waltz is quoted. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
